newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish quiet day mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish quiet day mixed.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished mixed after a quiet session spent waiting for FOMC meeting results.

The Federal Open Market Committee left key U.S. rates unchanged, and September Treasury bonds staged a brief reaction, popping to 114-14/32. But gains were soon pared and minutes after the announcement September returned to its earlier well-worn range. Traders noted that the long end was firm much of the day while the short end sagged.
"I guess the highlight was a curve flattening bias today," a Treasury bond futures trader said.
Another said players were unwinding curve steepeners from Friday. The first trader said he expected the curve to flatten a few basis points more.
But overall, the day was quiet as players watched action in U.S. stocks and waited for any new technical signs in September T-bonds.
Many traders have been eyeing 114-15/32 as a key technical level, and technicians have said how the market behaves around there was critical to the intermediate term trend.
The 114-15/32 level is the 50-percent retracement of the April to August rally.

"We've got the 114-15/32 retracement level, and I think we pretty much got there today," a T-bond futures trader said. "Maybe the lack of real followthrough (above 114-14/32) could lead to profit-taking tomorrow," he said.
But a 10-year notes trader said the firm close bodes well for the market near-term.
"We did close higher and we're at pretty critical levels and the market keeps absorbing a lot of selling here," he said. "I don't think we're done to the upside yet."
There was scant reaction to Redbook's 0.7-percent gain in U.S. adjusted retail sales in early August versus July.
At the close, September T-bonds were up 3/32 at 114-06/32, 10-year notes were flat at 109-23/32 and December Eurodollars were off 0.015 at 94.145. ((Chicago Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
